chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever says when he exits from the door of his house: 'I seek refuge with that with which the Angels of Allah seek refuge, from the evil of this new day which, when its sun sets, will not return, from the evil of myself, and from the evil of others, and from the evil of the Satans, and from the evil of the one who establishes hostility towards the Guardians of Allah, and from the evil of the Jinn and the humans, and from the evil of the predatory wild animals and the insects, and from the evil of indulging in the Prohibitions, all of them. I pledge myself with Allah from every evil. Allah will forgive him, turn to him, suffice him against worries, hold him back from evil, and protect him from harm.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when leaving the house for protection from evil?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication emphasizes the concept of 'Istia'dha' (seeking refuge) by aligning the believer's protection with that of the Angels, a practice rooted in the Shia tradition of daily spiritual armor. It comprehensively covers internal and external threats—from one's own self and Shayatin to enemies of the Awliya—promising divine forgiveness and relief from anxiety as a reward for consistent recitation.
